review_notes: I read the whole target file and the definitions it depends on: specIdeal, specIdeal_top and specIdeal_comap in CartierModule.lean, and ambientHyperplane, ambientHyperplane_chart and chart_linear_equation_radical in HyperplaneIdeal.lean. I also checked the PolyGrade and PolyChart abbreviations. The field, finiteness and Type-0 assumptions in the two hyperplane lemmas are real. Radicality of the linear equation needs a field, and Proj (PolyGrade K σ) is built over Type-level data. I judged that generalising them would need new mathematics, so I did not report them. comap_fromSpec is already universe-polymorphic, because R is not mentioned in it and so is not included from the variable line. The only unnecessary specialisation I found is the universe restriction in specIdeal_injective. I did not compile the proposed change. The proof only uses ΓSpecIso, map_map, map_id and inv_hom_id, all of which are universe-generic. The related specIdeal lemmas in CartierModule.lean already use R : Type u.

findings.excerpt:
variable {X : Scheme} {R : Type} [CommRing R]

lemma specIdeal_injective : Function.Injective (specIdeal (R := R)) := by
findings.problem: The lemma fixes `R : Type` (universe 0), but `specIdeal` is defined for `R : Type u` for any universe `u`. The proof uses only `specIdeal_top`, `Ideal.map_map`, `Ideal.map_id` and `Iso.inv_hom_id` of `Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of R)`, none of which depend on the universe. The restriction limits reuse to small rings. The `{X : Scheme}` binder is also an unused leftover in this variable line.
findings.proposed_change: Declare `universe u` and use `variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R]`. State `lemma specIdeal_injective : Function.Injective (specIdeal (R := R))` and keep the proof unchanged. This should elaborate, since `specIdeal` and `specIdeal_top` are already stated for `R : Type u`. Drop the unused `{X : Scheme}` from this variable line as well.
findings.benefit: The injectivity lemma then applies to rings in any universe, for example `Γ(X, U)` of a scheme `X : Scheme.{u}`. Its universe then matches the `specIdeal` API it belongs to, and users need no `ULift` or universe-0 workaround.
